title: Arawakan languages - Wikipedia
text: Arawakan, also known as Maipurean (also Maipuran), is a language family spoken amongst various Indigenous peoples in South America. Branches migrated to Central America and the Greater Antilles and Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean and the Atlantic, including what is now the Bahamas.

title: Saraveca language - Wikipedia
text: Saraveca (Xaray) [1] is an extinct Arawakan language once spoken in Bolivia by the Sarave. The language is known from about 400 words and a short text, and is closest to the Paresi language, spoken in Brazil.

title: Saraveca language — Grokipedia
text: Saraveca, also known as Saraveka or Xaray, is an extinct Arawakan language of the Maipurean branch, formerly spoken by the Sarave people in northern Bolivia near the eastern slopes of the Andes.
